events.title: FastAPI first released
events.summary: Sebastián Ramírez released FastAPI on December 5, 2018 — an async Python API framework with automatic OpenAPI docs.
events.about: FastAPI uses Python type hints and Pydantic for validation, Starlette for async I/O, and auto-generates Swagger UI docs. Used for ML inference APIs, microservices, and high-throughput backends. Example: `async def read_item(item_id: int)` with request/response schemas enforced at runtime and documented for free.

narrative.whyChosen: FastAPI became the default for new Python APIs when async and OpenAPI docs mattered.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed type hints could drive validation, serialization, and documentation in one cohesive framework.
narrative.problemSolved: Flask lacked native async and automatic API schemas; teams bolted on Marshmallow and manual Swagger.

events.title: Flutter 1.0 released
events.summary: Google released Flutter 1.0 on December 4, 2018 at Flutter Live — a UI toolkit for building native apps from a single Dart codebase.
events.about: Flutter compiles to native ARM code on iOS and Android with a custom rendering engine (Skia) — hot reload, Material/Cupertino widgets, and one codebase for mobile, web, and desktop. It became the main alternative to React Native for cross-platform mobile apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Flutter 1.0 made cross-platform native UI a Google-backed product, not an experiment.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved custom rendering could beat WebView bridges for mobile performance.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams maintained separate iOS and Android UIs or accepted hybrid WebView limitations.

events.title: WordPress 5.0 released
events.summary: WordPress 5.0 "Bebo" shipped on December 6, 2018 with Gutenberg — a block-based editor replacing the classic writing experience.
events.about: Gutenberg splits content into blocks (paragraphs, images, columns) edited in a React-powered UI — the biggest UX change in WordPress history. Themes and plugins adapted to block patterns; controversy drove the Classic Editor plugin, but blocks became the platform's future.

narrative.whyChosen: WordPress 5.0's Gutenberg editor redefined how millions publish content.
narrative.whyImportant: Block editing aligned WordPress with modern page builders and component-based UIs.
narrative.problemSolved: The classic TinyMCE editor could not compete with visual builders or structured content needs.

events.title: PyTorch 1.0 released
events.summary: Facebook AI Research released PyTorch 1.0 on December 7, 2018 at NeurIPS — adding production deployment via TorchScript and a stable API.
events.about: PyTorch 1.0 bridged research and production: `torch.jit.script` compiled models for C++ inference, and the Caffe2 backend merged into PyTorch for mobile deployment. It marked the framework's transition from academic toy to infrastructure for Meta, Tesla, and OpenAI training runs.

narrative.whyChosen: PyTorch 1.0 made the framework production-ready without sacrificing research ergonomics.
narrative.whyImportant: TorchScript and stable APIs let teams ship models trained in notebooks to serving infrastructure.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers loved PyTorch's flexibility but could not deploy models without rewriting in C++ or TensorFlow.
